name: הצגת וקטור כצירוף לינארי של שני וקטורים (באנגלית, ב)

functions.name: texp
functions.body: if numberp(x) and x<0 then concat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texsumf
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], concat("+",texp(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if numberp(t) and t<0 then concat("-",tex1(-t)) else concat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: cft
functions.body: concat(if c<0 then "-" else (if fst then "" else "+"), if abs(c)=1 then "" else tex1(abs(c)), tex1(s))

functions.name: texlin
functions.body: block([L:args(e), out:"", f:true], for k:1 thru length(L) step 2 do (if L[k]#0 then (out:concat(out, cft(L[k],L[k+1],f)), f:false)), if out="" then "0" else out)

questiontext:
Let \({\bf v_{1}}\), \({\bf v_2}\), \({\bf v_3}\) be the following vectors:

\[ {\bf v_{1}} = {{CT:0}},\quad {\bf v_{2}} = {{CT:1}},\quad {\bf v_{3}} = {{CT:2}}. \]

Find the values for \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) such that

\[{\bf v_3} = \lambda_1 {\bf v_1} + \lambda_2 {\bf v_2} .\]

If such values do not exist, enter zero for both entries.

\(\lambda_1\) = [[input:ans1]]      \(\lambda_2\) = [[input:ans2]]
[[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans2]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Comparing components gives 3 equations in 2 unknowns. A solution exists only if \({\bf v_3}\) is a combination of \({\bf v_1},{\bf v_2}\), and then the three vectors are linearly dependent and the determinant of the matrix whose columns they are is zero. Here the determinant is not zero, so there is no solution.
Step 1 — The linear system
If \({\bf v_3} = \lambda_1 {\bf v_1} + \lambda_2 {\bf v_2}\), each component of \({\bf v_3}\) is the same combination of the components of \({\bf v_1}\) and \({\bf v_2}\), so we have 3 equations in 2 unknowns:

\[ \begin{cases} {{CT:3}}={{CT:4}} \\ {{CT:5}}={{CT:6}} \\ {{CT:7}}={{CT:8}} \end{cases} \]

Step 2 — The determinant
If a solution existed, \({\bf v_3}-\lambda_1{\bf v_1}-\lambda_2{\bf v_2}={\bf 0}\) would be a nontrivial combination (the coefficient of \({\bf v_3}\) is 1), so \({\bf v_1},{\bf v_2},{\bf v_3}\) would be linearly dependent and the determinant of the matrix with these columns would be zero. The matrix is

\[ M={{CT:9}} \]

Expanding along the first row:

\[ \det M={{CT:10}}\begin{vmatrix} {{CT:11}} & {{CT:12}} \\ {{CT:13}} & {{CT:14}} \end{vmatrix}-{{CT:15}}\begin{vmatrix} {{CT:16}} & {{CT:12}} \\ {{CT:17}} & {{CT:14}} \end{vmatrix}+{{CT:18}}\begin{vmatrix} {{CT:16}} & {{CT:11}} \\ {{CT:17}} & {{CT:13}} \end{vmatrix} \]

\[ ={{CT:19}}-{{CT:20}}+{{CT:21}}={{CT:22}}={{CT:23}} \]

Step 3 — Conclusion
The determinant is \( {{CT:24}}\neq 0\), so the vectors are linearly independent, and \({\bf v_3}\) is not a combination of \({\bf v_1},{\bf v_2}\): there are no such \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\). As instructed, enter zero for both entries:

\[ \lambda_1 = 0,\qquad \lambda_2 = 0 \]
